questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to see something very different from my own country and meet a very different culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was a bit complicated to get all the paperwork done properly, so i had to email my own university a couple of times for help.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive any assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found it through a facebook page recommended by my erasmus coordinator in Heraklion. It was a bit difficult to find a proper place and I first stayed at a horrible place for a month where my landlord was spying on me and threatening me that she would call the police if I did not open the door whenever she wanted me to be home. So I was very frustrated and unhappy but I found a new place for the last two months, even though I had to pay overprice for a very small apartment.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Try and book through Airbnb or something that is not completely private because you don't know what you will get.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was hardly any help to find a place to stay and also there was no place where I could see where others lived, so I could get any recommendations.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: through their erasmus coordinator, and it worked very well

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Only the erasmus coordinator

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes i wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It works very well and they are helpfull

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A lot of the things were in greek and I could not understand a big part of it. Not all the doctors wanted to translate anything to us. The students were very kind and tried to translate things. Some of the doctors and young doctors tried to explain things to us and include os, while some of the doctors only ignored us and many of the students were almost afraid of some of the doctors. Some of the doctors wanted to explain a lot of things to us, but they were also very busy so there were days where we did not speak to a single doctor. One of the doctors from the orthopedics department just called me "the blond girl" and refused to lean my name, and also in my presence spoke in greek calling my country (Denmark) the most racist country in Europe. I did not understand what he said at that time but afterwards the greek students translated it to me.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: the level was pretty close to my own level. Maybe a bit higher because i followed a lot of students in their 2. year of their master, while I was in my first year of my master.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I did not attend any classes but when the doctor explained some things for us, we were often 3-10 students pr. doctor. Compared to UCPH you are always just one student pr. doctor.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: i had a clinical rotation in cardiology, gastroenterology and orthopedics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: cardiology was the best. The main professor spoke a lot in English and translated a lot of things. Also the young doctor i followed was very good.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: an extra sim card, a higher rent because i had to move during my stay and for the bus tickets

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: food is cheap compared to Denmark, my apartment was quite expensive. The flight tickets were expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: there were hikes, game nights, bowling nights, boat trips, beach trips, parties and "the Crete trip". The social part was absolutely amazing!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of the things above, go to the beaches, visit the cities and rent a car and drive around the island. Go hiking and on boat trips and participate in the different activities arranged by the greek students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: travel around the island -not only to the bigger cities but also to smaller ones for instance in the south.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: very easy, except the stores are all closed on Sundays and many of the shops are closed from 1-2 pm and open again in the night around 5-6 pm.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: talk to all the greek medical students in the hospital -they are so kind!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Non, except my first landlord being controlling because I'm a girl and the doctor in orthopedics that made jokes about women becoming doctors in that field.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the social part, meeting up any time of the day, on a beach or in a cafe and just having fun

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) don't expect to lean what you lean in a hospital in Denmark -you go to Greece to see something different so you will also lean something different (but you will still be able to make it through your exams in Denmark without problems like the OSCE)
2) Meet as many people you can and have fun with them. There are so many students from so many different countries so it is like a gift to get that many friends from all over Europe.
3) Take time to see the island, not only the bigger cites but also smaller ones, local places and rent a car so you can go anywhere you want.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't be afraid of speaking in English -we all have a different mother language (or many of us) so we all make mistakes. But being afraid of speaking in English will make you miss a lot of opportunities.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To have met so many nice people from so many different countries.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having to move during my stay, after my first month because I was afraid that my landlord would call the police if I did not do as she said and also being afraid that she would be violent towards me.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Have fun! You will never regret your exchange!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
